sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Text 1: Psychologists long held that willpower works like a muscle: using self-control on one task drains a limited supply, leaving less self-control for the next task. Text 2: Researchers who repeated the classic willpower experiments in dozens of laboratories found little or no drop in self-control after participants completed an initial demanding task. Based on the texts, how would the researchers in Text 2 most likely describe the view presented in Text 1?

options.a: As a view that their experiments confirmed in nearly every laboratory that took part
options.b: As a view that applies to physical exercise but not to mental tasks like self-control
options.c: As a view that their large-scale attempts to repeat earlier results did not support
options.d: As a view that had never been tested in experiments before their own studies began

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Text 2 reports that repeating the classic experiments across many labs produced 'little or no drop' in self-control. Those researchers would therefore say their replication attempts did not support the willpower-as-muscle view.

distractorExplanations.a: Reverses the finding: the labs found little or no effect, so they did not confirm the view.
distractorExplanations.b: Neither text discusses physical exercise; the muscle idea in Text 1 is only a comparison.
distractorExplanations.d: Text 2 says the researchers repeated 'classic' experiments, so the view had been tested before.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Text 1: Art critic Hana Osei praises the city's new public murals for bringing bold color to neglected neighborhoods and inviting residents to see their streets differently. Text 2: Community organizer Luis Ortega agrees that the murals are striking, but he notes that residents were never consulted about their subjects; several murals depict scenes that have little to do with the neighborhoods' history. Based on the texts, on which point would Osei and Ortega most likely agree?

options.a: The murals reflect the history of the neighborhoods in which they appear.
options.b: The murals are visually striking additions to the city's neighborhoods.
options.c: The murals were designed with extensive input from local residents.
options.d: The murals should be painted over and replaced with new artwork.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Osei praises the murals' bold color, and Ortega 'agrees that the murals are striking' before raising his concern. Their shared ground is that the murals are visually impressive.

distractorExplanations.a: Ortega says several murals have little to do with the neighborhoods' history, so he would disagree.
distractorExplanations.c: Ortega says residents were never consulted, which contradicts this choice.
distractorExplanations.d: Neither writer calls for removing the murals; Ortega criticizes the process, not the art's existence.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Text 1: Some ecologists argue that reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 caused elk to avoid riverbanks, allowing willow and aspen trees there to recover. Text 2: Ecologist Ingrid Dahl acknowledges that willows have recovered in parts of the park, but she points out that elk numbers also fell sharply because of hunting outside the park and harsh winters during the same years. She argues that the trees' recovery cannot be credited to wolves alone. Based on the texts, how would Dahl most likely respond to the ecologists in Text 1?

options.a: By denying that willow and aspen trees have recovered in any part of the park since 1995
options.b: By noting that other changes in the same period may also explain the trees' recovery
options.c: By arguing that wolves increased the elk population by removing weak and sick animals
options.d: By claiming that hunting should be banned near the park to protect the willow trees

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Dahl accepts that willows recovered but names other causes at work at the same time (hunting, harsh winters). Her response to Text 1 is that wolves may not be the whole explanation.

distractorExplanations.a: Dahl 'acknowledges that willows have recovered,' so she does not deny the recovery.
distractorExplanations.c: Dahl says elk numbers fell, which contradicts the claim that wolves increased them.
distractorExplanations.d: Dahl mentions hunting as a cause of fewer elk; she makes no policy proposal.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Text 1: Many teachers require handwritten notes, arguing that students who write by hand remember lecture material better than students who type. Text 2: Education researcher Sam Patel found that the advantage disappeared when typing students were told to summarize ideas in their own words instead of copying the lecture word for word. Based on the texts, what would Patel most likely say about the benefit described in Text 1?

options.a: It appears only when students take notes on paper rather than on a laptop.
options.b: It comes from how students process the material, not from handwriting itself.
options.c: It is larger for students who copy lectures word for word than for others.
options.d: It disappears when teachers allow students to record each lecture on video.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Patel found that typists who summarized in their own words remembered as well as handwriters. That suggests the benefit comes from processing ideas, which handwriting happens to encourage, rather than from the pen itself.

distractorExplanations.a: Patel showed typists could match the benefit, so it is not limited to paper.
distractorExplanations.c: Copying word for word is the habit Patel's instructions removed to close the gap; it is not linked to a larger benefit.
distractorExplanations.d: Video recording is never mentioned in either text.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • The Atacama Desert in Chile is one of the driest places on Earth. • Some weather stations there have recorded almost no rain for decades. • Its dry, clear skies make it a leading site for astronomical observatories. • The Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) is located there. The student wants to explain why astronomers build observatories in the Atacama Desert. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: The Atacama Desert in Chile, home to the ALMA observatory, is one of the driest places anywhere on Earth.
options.b: Some weather stations in Chile's Atacama Desert have recorded almost no rain at all for several decades.
options.c: The Atacama Large Millimeter Array, known as ALMA, is an observatory located in Chile's Atacama Desert.
options.d: Its dry, clear skies make Chile's Atacama Desert a leading site for observatories such as ALMA.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The goal asks why observatories are built there, so the sentence must give a reason. Only this choice states the reason from the notes (dry, clear skies) and links it to observatories.

distractorExplanations.a: Mentions dryness and ALMA but never connects dryness to why observatories are built there.
distractorExplanations.b: Gives a rainfall fact with no mention of astronomy or observatories.
distractorExplanations.c: States where ALMA is located but not why astronomers chose the desert.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Sea otters and beavers are both mammals that spend much of their lives in water. • Sea otters live in coastal ocean waters of the North Pacific. • Beavers live in freshwater rivers, streams, and ponds. • Sea otters stay warm with extremely dense fur; beavers rely on fur and a layer of fat. The student wants to contrast the habitats of the two animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Sea otters and beavers are both mammals that spend a large part of their lives swimming in the water.
options.b: While sea otters live in coastal waters of the North Pacific, beavers live in freshwater rivers, streams, and ponds.
options.c: Sea otters stay warm with very dense fur, while beavers rely on a combination of fur and a layer of fat.
options.d: Beavers, which are mammals, live in freshwater rivers, streams, and ponds and spend much of their lives in water.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The goal combines two requirements: a contrast, and habitats. Only this choice contrasts where each animal lives (coastal ocean versus freshwater), using 'while' to mark the difference.

distractorExplanations.a: States a similarity between the animals, not a contrast.
distractorExplanations.c: Draws a contrast, but about how the animals stay warm rather than where they live.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes only the beaver's habitat, so nothing is contrasted.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Chinua Achebe was a Nigerian novelist. • His novel Things Fall Apart was published in 1958. • It follows Okonkwo, a leader in an Igbo village, as colonial rule and missionaries arrive. • The novel has been translated into more than 50 languages. The student wants to introduce the novel and its author to an audience unfamiliar with both. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Things Fall Apart (1958), by Nigerian novelist Chinua Achebe, follows an Igbo village leader as colonial rule arrives.
options.b: Things Fall Apart has been translated into more than 50 languages since it was first published in 1958.
options.c: Achebe's novel follows the village leader Okonkwo as missionaries and colonial rule arrive in his Igbo community.
options.d: Chinua Achebe, who wrote Things Fall Apart, was a novelist whose work has been widely translated around the world.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: An unfamiliar audience needs to know who the author is and what the novel is about. This choice identifies the author (Nigerian novelist Chinua Achebe), the title and date, and the basic story.

distractorExplanations.b: Gives the novel's reach but never identifies the author or the story.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses 'Achebe' as if readers already know him and never explains who he is.
distractorExplanations.d: Identifies the author but says nothing about what the novel is about.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911. • Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962. • Both are among the few people to have won two Nobel Prizes. The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Curie and Pauling. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in both Physics and Chemistry, in 1903 and 1911 respectively.
options.b: Like Marie Curie, who won Nobel Prizes in 1903 and 1911, Linus Pauling won two Nobel Prizes.
options.c: Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954, more than forty years after Curie's second prize.
options.d: Curie's two prizes were both in science, whereas one of Pauling's prizes was the Nobel Peace Prize.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: A similarity needs both people and the shared trait. 'Like Marie Curie… Linus Pauling won two Nobel Prizes' names both and states what they have in common.

distractorExplanations.a: Describes only Curie, so no similarity is shown.
distractorExplanations.c: Emphasizes the gap in time between their prizes, a difference rather than a similarity.
distractorExplanations.d: Uses 'whereas' to highlight a difference in the kinds of prizes they won.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Researcher Clara Voss studied whether background music affects reading comprehension. • She had 120 students read passages either in silence or with instrumental music playing. • All students then answered the same comprehension questions. • Students who read in silence scored 8% higher on average. The student wants to describe the method of Voss's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Students who read in silence scored 8% higher on comprehension questions than students who read with music.
options.b: Voss had 120 students read passages in silence or with instrumental music, then answer the same questions.
options.c: Clara Voss wanted to find out whether background music affects how well students understand what they read.
options.d: According to a study of 120 students by researcher Clara Voss, background music may lower reading comprehension.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: A method describes what the researcher did: who took part, what conditions they experienced, and how they were measured. This choice gives all three (120 students, silence versus music, the same questions).

distractorExplanations.a: Reports the study's result, not how the study was carried out.
distractorExplanations.c: States the research question, not the procedure used to answer it.
distractorExplanations.d: States the conclusion; mentioning 120 students does not describe the procedure.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • A city installed 400 streetlights with brighter LED bulbs in 2021. • The city tracked nighttime car accidents for two years before and two years after the change. • Nighttime accidents on the relit streets fell by 21%. • Accidents on streets without the new lights stayed about the same. The student wants to present the study's findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: In 2021, the city installed 400 new streetlights fitted with brighter LED bulbs and began tracking accidents.
options.b: After the new lights went in, nighttime accidents on those streets fell 21%, while other streets saw little change.
options.c: The city tracked nighttime car accidents for two years before and two years after installing the new lights.
options.d: Streets without the new lights served as a comparison group during the city's two years of accident tracking.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Findings are what the data showed. This choice reports the 21% drop on relit streets and the lack of change elsewhere, the two results in the notes.

distractorExplanations.a: Describes the change the city made, not what the tracking found.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes how data were collected, which is method rather than findings.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes the comparison design but leaves out what the comparison showed.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Tardigrades are microscopic animals about 0.5 millimeters long. • They can survive being dried out for years by entering a state called cryptobiosis. • In 2007, tardigrades survived exposure to open space on a European Space Agency mission. • Studying how they survive drying out may help scientists protect cells and vaccines from damage. The student wants to emphasize the practical value of studying tardigrades. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Tardigrades, microscopic animals about half a millimeter long, survived exposure to open space in 2007.
options.b: By entering a state called cryptobiosis, tardigrades can survive being completely dried out for years.
options.c: Learning how tardigrades survive drying out could help scientists protect cells and vaccines from damage.
options.d: Tardigrades are microscopic animals that took part in a 2007 European Space Agency mission to open space.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Practical value means a real-world use. Only this choice connects tardigrade research to a use (protecting cells and vaccines).

distractorExplanations.a: An impressive fact about survival in space, but it names no practical application.
distractorExplanations.b: Explains how tardigrades survive drying, not why studying them is useful.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes the space mission without any practical benefit of the research.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece. • They took place in 1896. • About 240 athletes from 14 nations competed. • Events included athletics, cycling, swimming, and wrestling. The student wants to indicate when and where the first modern Olympic Games were held. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: About 240 athletes from 14 nations competed in the first modern Olympic Games.
options.b: The first modern Olympics included athletics, cycling, swimming, and wrestling.
options.c: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
options.d: Athletes from 14 nations competed in events such as cycling and wrestling in Athens.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The goal names two details: when and where. Only this choice gives both the place (Athens, Greece) and the year (1896).

distractorExplanations.a: Gives the number of athletes and nations but neither the date nor the place.
distractorExplanations.b: Lists events, which answers neither when nor where.
distractorExplanations.d: Names the place but leaves out the year.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: • Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometers between Canada and central Mexico. • Arctic terns migrate between the Arctic and the Antarctic each year. • Gray whales travel between Arctic feeding waters and breeding lagoons in Mexico. • Many animals migrate long distances to reach food or breeding grounds. The student wants to make a generalization about animal migration. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.a: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometers each year between Canada and central Mexico.
options.b: Many animals, from butterflies to whales, migrate long distances to reach food or breeding grounds.
options.c: Arctic terns migrate between the Arctic and the Antarctic, crossing nearly the entire globe each year.
options.d: Gray whales travel each year between their Arctic feeding waters and breeding lagoons in Mexico.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: A generalization makes a broad statement about many cases. This choice states a pattern across many animals ('Many animals… migrate long distances') and uses the examples only to show its range.

distractorExplanations.a: Describes one species, which is a specific example rather than a generalization.
distractorExplanations.c: Describes one species' route and adds a detail not in the notes.
distractorExplanations.d: Describes one species, so it does not generalize about migration.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Glass is often thought of as fragile. ______ certain types of treated glass are strong enough to serve as the floors of observation decks hundreds of meters above the ground. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The first sentence states a common belief (glass is fragile), and the second shows glass strong enough to walk on high above the ground. That contrast calls for 'However.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'Therefore' signals a result, but strong glass does not follow from glass being fragile.
distractorExplanations.c: 'Similarly' signals a matching idea, but the sentences contrast.
distractorExplanations.d: Strong glass is not an example of fragility; it contradicts it.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The bakery switched to locally grown flour last spring. ______ its bread now varies slightly in flavor from one harvest to the next, something regular customers say they have come to enjoy. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Local flour changes with each harvest, so bread made from it changes too. The second sentence is an effect of the first, which calls for 'As a result.'

distractorExplanations.a: Nothing is being contrasted; the flavor change follows from the switch.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Nevertheless' signals a surprise despite the first sentence, but the change is expected.
distractorExplanations.d: The flavor change is a consequence of the switch, not an example of it.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Octopuses can change the color of their skin in a fraction of a second. ______ they can alter its texture, raising small bumps to mimic the surface of rocks or coral. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Changing texture is a second, additional camouflage ability alongside changing color. An addition transition such as 'Moreover' fits.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Instead' implies texture change replaces color change, but octopuses can do both.
distractorExplanations.b: Texture change is not caused by color change; it is a separate ability.
distractorExplanations.c: 'Even so' signals a contrast or concession, but the two abilities support each other.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Early critics praised the film's striking visuals. Its plot, ______ was widely dismissed as confusing and slow. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Praise for the visuals is followed by criticism of the plot. A contrast transition, 'however,' is needed even though it sits in the middle of the sentence.

distractorExplanations.a: The plot's weakness is not a result of the strong visuals.
distractorExplanations.b: A dismissed plot is not an example of praised visuals.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Similarly' signals agreement, but praise and dismissal are opposites.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Many desert plants store water in thick stems or leaves. The saguaro cactus, ______ can expand its pleated trunk to hold hundreds of liters of water after a single heavy rain. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The first sentence makes a general statement about desert plants storing water; the saguaro is one specific case of it. 'For example' introduces an illustration.

distractorExplanations.a: The saguaro supports the first sentence rather than contrasting with it.
distractorExplanations.c: 'By comparison' sets the saguaro apart from other plants, but it is an instance of the same behavior.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Meanwhile' signals something happening at the same time, which does not fit here.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Researchers expected the new fertilizer to increase wheat yields. ______ yields in the treated fields were slightly lower than in untreated fields, prompting the team to rethink its hypothesis. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The result (lower yields) is the opposite of what researchers expected. 'Surprisingly' marks an outcome that goes against expectations.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Accordingly' signals a result that matches the first sentence, but the yields went the other way.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Likewise' signals similarity, but the result contradicts the expectation.
distractorExplanations.c: 'In particular' introduces a specific detail of the first idea, not a reversal.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: To make the dye, workers first soak the plant's roots in water for several days. ______ they boil the softened roots to release a deep red color. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The text describes steps in a process, and 'first' signals that a later step follows. 'Next' continues the sequence.

distractorExplanations.b: 'Nonetheless' signals a concession, but boiling simply follows soaking.
distractorExplanations.c: Boiling is a new step, not a restatement of soaking.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Conversely' signals an opposite, but the two steps work together.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The ancient city of Petra was carved directly into rose-colored sandstone cliffs. ______ its builders did not need to haul stone from distant quarries; the material for their temples and tombs was already in place. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Because the city was carved from the cliffs themselves, no stone had to be transported. The second sentence is a consequence of the first, so 'Thus' fits.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Still' signals a contrast or concession, but the second sentence follows logically from the first.
distractorExplanations.c: 'Meanwhile' signals simultaneous events, not a consequence.
distractorExplanations.d: There is no contrast; not hauling stone is explained by carving into existing rock.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The novelist rarely gave interviews, and fans had waited years for a chance to hear her speak. ______ when she agreed to appear at a small library in her hometown, tickets sold out within minutes. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Years of rare appearances built up demand, which explains why tickets sold out so fast. The second sentence is a result of the first, so 'Consequently' fits.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Similarly' signals a parallel idea, but the sellout is caused by the demand described first.
distractorExplanations.b: The sellout is not an example of her rarely giving interviews.
distractorExplanations.c: 'In particular' narrows to a detail of the previous idea rather than stating its result.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The glacier has retreated nearly two kilometers since ______ scientists expect it to shrink further as summers grow warmer. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Both parts are independent clauses ('The glacier has retreated…' and 'scientists expect…'). A semicolon can join two independent clauses without a conjunction.

distractorExplanations.a: A comma alone between two independent clauses creates a comma splice.
distractorExplanations.c: With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together as a fused sentence.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Which' would need to refer to a noun, but 'which scientists expect it to shrink' leaves the clause incomplete.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The traditional recipe calls for only three ______ flour, water, and salt. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete independent clause. 'The traditional recipe calls for only three ingredients' is complete, and the list explains it.

distractorExplanations.a: A semicolon must join two independent clauses, but 'flour, water, and salt' is just a list.
distractorExplanations.b: 'These are flour…' is an independent clause, so joining it with only a comma creates a comma splice.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Which flour, water, and salt' has no verb, so the sentence becomes ungrammatical.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The researchers who developed the new ______ that it could power a small car for more than 500 kilometers on a single charge. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The subject is 'The researchers who developed the new battery' and the verb is 'claim.' No punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb, even when the subject is long.

distractorExplanations.a: A single comma between the subject and its verb is not allowed.
distractorExplanations.c: A semicolon needs an independent clause on each side, and the subject alone is not one.
distractorExplanations.d: A colon must follow a complete independent clause; here it splits the subject from its verb.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Ada Lovelace ______ wrote what many historians consider the first published computer program in the 1840s. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.a: the daughter of the poet Lord Byron,
options.b: , the daughter of the poet Lord Byron,
options.c: , who was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron
options.d: ; the daughter of the poet Lord Byron;

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'The daughter of the poet Lord Byron' is extra information about Lovelace (a nonrestrictive appositive), so it must be set off by a matching pair of commas, one before and one after.

distractorExplanations.a: The opening comma is missing, so the appositive is not properly set off.
distractorExplanations.c: The closing comma is missing after 'Byron', so the clause runs into the verb 'wrote'.
distractorExplanations.d: Semicolons cannot set off an appositive; they join independent clauses.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The island's only road—a narrow gravel track built in the ______ floods nearly every spring. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The interruption opens with a dash after 'road,' so it must close with a matching dash before the verb 'floods.' Paired punctuation must match.

distractorExplanations.a: A comma cannot close an interruption that opened with a dash.
distractorExplanations.b: Without a closing dash, the interruption runs straight into the main verb.
distractorExplanations.d: Adding 'and' leaves the dash unclosed and gives the subject 'road' no main verb of its own.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Although the museum closed for renovations in ______ its outdoor sculpture garden remained open to visitors throughout the spring. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Although the museum closed for renovations in March' is a dependent clause introducing the main clause. A comma separates an introductory dependent clause from the independent clause that follows.

distractorExplanations.a: A semicolon cannot follow a dependent clause; it needs an independent clause on each side.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Although' already links the clauses, so adding 'and' makes the sentence ungrammatical.
distractorExplanations.c: A period leaves 'Although… March' as a sentence fragment.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Honeybees communicate the location of food through a movement called the waggle ______ angle of the dance indicates the direction of the food relative to the sun. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Each part is an independent clause. A period correctly separates them into two sentences.

distractorExplanations.b: A comma alone between two independent clauses is a comma splice.
distractorExplanations.c: No punctuation fuses the two independent clauses into a run-on sentence.
distractorExplanations.d: A comma is not used after the conjunction 'and' here; the extra comma breaks the clause.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The touring exhibit will visit Lyon, ______ Porto, Portugal; and Turin, Italy. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: When list items already contain commas (city, country), semicolons separate the items. The other items are separated by semicolons, so 'France' needs one too.

distractorExplanations.a: A comma here would blur where one city-country pair ends and the next begins.
distractorExplanations.c: With no punctuation, 'France Porto' runs two list items together.
distractorExplanations.d: 'And' belongs only before the final item, and a comma breaks the semicolon pattern.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Only the students ______ must submit an extra report; everyone else has already finished the assignment. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The clause 'who missed the field trip' identifies which students must submit the report, so it is restrictive (essential) and takes no commas.

distractorExplanations.b: Commas would mark the clause as extra information, but it is needed to say which students are meant.
distractorExplanations.c: An opening comma without a closing one separates the essential clause and the subject incorrectly.
distractorExplanations.d: A comma between the subject phrase and the verb 'must submit' is not allowed.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The expedition's supplies ______ tents, camp stoves, and enough food for three weeks. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The list is the object of the verb 'included,' and no punctuation goes between a verb and its object.

distractorExplanations.a: A colon must follow a complete independent clause; 'The expedition's supplies included' is not complete.
distractorExplanations.c: A semicolon would cut the verb off from its object.
distractorExplanations.d: A dash would separate the verb from its object without any reason.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The committee is still debating whether the new park should include a dog ______ Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Whether the new park should include a dog run' is an indirect question inside a statement. The sentence is a statement, so it ends with a period.

distractorExplanations.a: An indirect question does not take a question mark; the sentence states what is being debated.
distractorExplanations.b: A comma cannot end a sentence; the statement is complete after 'run' and needs a period.
distractorExplanations.d: A semicolon cannot end a sentence.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Exhausted after the long ______ the hikers rested beside the lake before starting down the mountain. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Exhausted after the long climb' is an introductory participial phrase describing the hikers. A comma separates it from the main clause.

distractorExplanations.a: A semicolon needs an independent clause before it, but the opening phrase is not one.
distractorExplanations.b: A period leaves 'Exhausted after the long climb' as a fragment.
distractorExplanations.c: 'And' cannot join a descriptive phrase to an independent clause.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The list of required documents for the scholarship application ______ posted on the city's website. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The subject is 'list' (singular); 'of required documents' is a prepositional phrase that does not change the subject. A singular subject takes the singular verb 'is.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'Are' agrees with 'documents,' which is inside the prepositional phrase, not with the subject 'list.'
distractorExplanations.b: 'Were' is plural and agrees with 'documents' instead of 'list.'
distractorExplanations.d: 'Have been' is plural and does not agree with the singular subject 'list.'

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: When the orchestra finished ______ final piece, the audience rose to its feet and applauded for several minutes. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Orchestra' is a singular collective noun acting as one group, so it takes the singular possessive pronoun 'its' (no apostrophe).

distractorExplanations.a: 'Their' is plural and does not agree with the singular noun 'orchestra.'
distractorExplanations.c: 'It's' is a contraction of 'it is,' not a possessive.
distractorExplanations.d: 'They're' is a contraction of 'they are' and is plural.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: By the time the rescue team arrived at the ridge, the stranded hikers ______ for nearly six hours. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The waiting happened before another past event (the team arrived). An action completed before a past moment takes the past perfect, 'had waited.'

distractorExplanations.b: Present tense clashes with the past-tense time marker 'arrived.'
distractorExplanations.c: Future perfect describes an action completed before a future moment, not a past one.
distractorExplanations.d: Present progressive does not fit an event already finished in the past.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Hoping to finish the mural before the festival, ______ Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.a: the night was spent working by the artists.
options.b: the artists worked through the night.
options.c: working through the night was the artists' plan.
options.d: the mural was painted by the artists overnight.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: An introductory modifier describes the noun that comes right after the comma. The artists are the ones hoping to finish, so 'the artists' must follow the modifier.

distractorExplanations.a: This says the night was hoping to finish the mural, a dangling modifier.
distractorExplanations.c: This makes 'working' the one hoping to finish, which is illogical.
distractorExplanations.d: This says the mural was hoping to finish itself before the festival.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The ______ nests, each built from mud and saliva by a different pair of birds, cling to the cliff walls in tight clusters. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The nests belong to many swallows (each built by a different pair). The plural possessive of 'swallows' is formed by adding only an apostrophe: 'swallows'.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'Swallow's' is singular possessive, but the nests belong to many birds.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Swallows' without an apostrophe is a plain plural and does not show possession.
distractorExplanations.d: A plural noun ending in s does not take an extra 's after the apostrophe.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Along the edge of the old harbor ______ a single row of brightly painted fishing huts. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject comes after the verb. The subject is 'row' (singular), not 'huts,' so the verb must be singular: 'stands.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'Stand' is plural and agrees with 'huts,' which belongs to the phrase 'of… fishing huts.'
distractorExplanations.b: 'Are standing' is plural and does not agree with the singular subject 'row.'
distractorExplanations.c: 'Have stood' is plural and does not agree with 'row.'

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: Neither of the two bridges into town ______ open to traffic during the storm, so residents had to wait until morning. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Neither' is the subject and is singular; 'of the two bridges' does not change that. The past setting ('during the storm,' 'had to wait') also requires past tense, so 'was' is correct.

distractorExplanations.a: 'Were' is plural and agrees with 'bridges' instead of the singular subject 'neither.'
distractorExplanations.c: 'Are' is plural and present tense, which clashes with both the subject and the past setting.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Have been' is plural and present perfect, which does not fit a past event.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The ancient manuscript had ______ forgotten in a monastery library for centuries before scholars recognized its importance. Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: 'Lie' (to rest) takes no object; its past participle is 'lain.' After 'had,' the past participle is needed: 'had lain.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'Laid' is the past participle of 'lay' (to put something down), which needs an object.
distractorExplanations.c: 'Lay' is the simple past of 'lie,' not the past participle required after 'had.'
distractorExplanations.d: 'Laying' comes from 'lay,' which needs an object; the manuscript was resting, not placing anything.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: The new library offers quiet study rooms, a makerspace with 3D printers, and ______ Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

options.a: it has a café that stays open late.
options.b: staying open late in its café.
options.c: a café that stays open late.
options.d: because its café stays open late.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Items in a list must share the same grammatical form. The first two items are noun phrases (rooms, a makerspace), so the third must be one too: 'a café.'

distractorExplanations.a: 'It has a café' is an independent clause, breaking the list of noun phrases.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Staying open late' is a verb phrase, not a noun phrase like the other items.
distractorExplanations.d: 'Because…' is a dependent clause, which does not fit a list of things the library offers.

sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.prompt: During the last decade, the population of Harlow County grew faster than ______ Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
sat-readiness-check-reading-and-writing-.explanation: Comparisons must match like with like: one county's population with another county's population. 'That of any neighboring county' means 'the population of any neighboring county' and is singular, matching 'population.'

distractorExplanations.a: Compares a population with a county, which is an illogical comparison.
distractorExplanations.b: 'Those' is plural, but it stands for the singular noun 'population.'
distractorExplanations.d: 'County's had' leaves the possessive without a noun and uses the wrong verb form.
